chunks: And how many a prophet fought alongside him were many seekers (of God), so they did not weaken for what befall them in the way of Allah, nor did they become weak, nor did they submit, and Allah loves the steadfast.

key_terms.اسْتَكَانُوا: They submitted or gave up humbly
key_terms.الصَّابِرِينَ: The steadfast; those who practice patience and perseverance
key_terms.رِبِّيُّونَ: Seekers of God; plural of rabbani, referring to those devoted to divine learning and teaching
key_terms.ضَعُفُوا: They became physically or militarily weak
key_terms.وَهَنُوا: They weakened in spirit or resolve

ai.seo_question: How did the prophets and their companions respond to hardships in the way of God?
ai.summary: In Shia exegesis, this verse is often linked to the era of the Prophet Muhammad and the Twelve Imams, illustrating that spiritual strength (qawwa) is not diminished by physical trials or military setbacks. It underscores the concept of sabr (steadfast patience) as an active, resilient endurance rather than passive suffering, affirming divine love for those who remain firm in their covenant despite adversity.
